title: System Setup and Initialisation
description: The TDPO learns to set up the DP simulator correctly from scratch on every session. Professional standard means every field populated accurately, every sensor confirmed, every thruster enabled, and a clean steady-state before any drill begins.

tasks.title: Full System Setup From Scratch
tasks.setup: Cold screen. No pre-configuration. Start from the beginning.
tasks.execute: Complete the full simulator setup procedure without using any guide. Enter real vessel position from GPS display, heading from gyrocompass, draft from stability display, water depth from echosounder. Confirm all sensors active and healthy. Confirm all thrusters enabled. Set environment to calm. Run a 3-minute steady state check — vessel must hold position with minimal thruster activity before you declare setup complete.
professional_standard: All fields correctly populated from live vessel data
All sensors showing green — no rejections or warnings
All thrusters enabled and showing in schematic
Vessel stable after 3-minute steady state check

fields.label: Any items missed or incorrect on first attempt
Sensor status at completion — all green?
Thruster status at completion — all enabled?
Steady state check result — vessel stable?

debrief_questions: What would happen to the vessel model if you entered the wrong water depth — how does an incorrect depth affect the simulation?
Why must the initial heading entered match the actual vessel heading precisely — what goes wrong if it does not?
What does the 3-minute steady state check confirm — and what does it tell you if the vessel is not stable?
Which sensor is most critical for DP position keeping and why?
If one gyro was showing a 2 degree difference from the other at setup — would you proceed? What would you do and why?
model_answers: Depth feeds the current and shallow-water model. Enter a depth much greater than actual and the model under-estimates the current force and the sluggish shallow-water response, so the controller's feed-forward is wrong before anything else happens: the vessel sits with a steady offset the DPO cannot explain, and thruster demand does not match what the sea state suggests it should be. Too shallow and the model over-reacts. The point is that the whole simulation is only as good as what was typed in — a wrong depth is not a small error, it invalidates the exercise.

The controller resolves thruster demand into vessel axes using heading. If the entered heading is wrong by even a few degrees, the model's idea of where the bow is points somewhere the vessel is not, so surge demand leaks into sway and the vessel walks off track while the display reports it holding. On the reference vessel, heading is 000° True at setup and the entered value must match the gyro exactly. Wind feed-forward is resolved the same way, so a heading error also puts the wind correction on the wrong axis.

It confirms the vessel has reached equilibrium — that thruster output is balancing the environment and not chasing an error the DPO introduced. On the reference vessel in calm conditions expect low, steady demand on the tunnels with the mains trimming, and position and heading holding within a metre and a fraction of a degree. If it is not stable, something entered at setup is wrong or a sensor is feeding bad data: the answer is to find that cause, not to start the drill and hope it settles.

Position reference is what DP cannot run without — with no accepted reference the system has nothing to close the loop on and drops to a heading-and-thruster-only mode. But the honest answer names the gyro alongside it: heading is used to resolve every reference and every thruster command into vessel axes, so a gyro fault corrupts good position data as well. On the reference vessel, two DGPS and two gyros mean neither is a single point of failure, and that redundancy is the reason for the pairing.

No. Two degrees is far outside the half-degree agreement expected at setup, and with only two gyros there is no third to vote on which one is right. Report it to the supervising DPO, check both against a known bearing or the vessel's heading on a reference before accepting either, and do not start a drill until the disagreement is understood. Proceeding on a wrongly-resolved heading means every observation recorded that session is against a model that was never correct.

model_outcome.time_to_complete_minutes: 10–15 for a competent first pass; under 10 by the end of the 30 days
model_outcome.items_missed_first_attempt: Typically none by day 3; draft and water depth are the two most often left at default
model_outcome.sensor_status_at_completion: All green — both DGPS accepted with SNR above 35, both gyros within 0.5°, both wind sensors active, both VRUs healthy
model_outcome.thruster_status_at_completion: All five enabled and shown in the schematic — two bow tunnel, one stern tunnel, two main azimuth aft
model_outcome.steady_state_result: Stable: position held within 1 m and heading within 0.5° over the 3 minutes, with low steady thruster demand and no rejections
model_outcome.notes: Bus tie open with one bow tunnel and one main on each board — confirm the split before declaring setup complete

variants.title: Setup Against the Clock
variants.note_to_tdpo: Same setup, harder target. A professional DPO can set up efficiently. Aim for 10 minutes without sacrificing accuracy.

variants.title: Setup With One Deliberate Error
variants.note_to_tdpo: Your DPO will introduce one deliberate misconfiguration during setup. Find it before starting any drill. This simulates inheriting a badly configured desk.

tasks.title: Checklist Discipline
tasks.setup: Paper and pen only. App closed.
tasks.execute: Before opening the app, write down every item on the pre-session checklist from memory. All 16 items, in order, with a one-sentence explanation of why each item matters. Then open the app and compare your list. Note any items missed, any items in wrong order, any explanations that were incomplete.
professional_standard: Recall minimum 14 of 16 items without reference
Correct explanation for each item recalled

fields.label: Items recalled but in wrong order
Which item was hardest to explain and why?

debrief_questions: Which checklist items have the highest immediate safety significance if skipped?
What is the consequence of starting a drill with a reference system misconfigured?
Why does the checklist require DPO presence to be confirmed before anything else — not after setup?
If you could only check five items due to time pressure, which five would you choose and why?

variants.title: Checklist From Memory — No Mistakes
variants.note_to_tdpo: All 16 items, correct order, correct explanation. This is the standard a DPO would expect before signing off Section 1 of your logbook.
